brain.name: Brain
brain.description: The brain is the central organ of the nervous system. It receives and processes information from the body, controls movement, emotions, memory, learning, consciousness, and regulates essential life functions.
anatomy: Cerebrum - responsible for thinking, memory, reasoning and voluntary movement
Cerebellum - coordinates balance and muscle movements
Brainstem - controls breathing, heartbeat and vital functions
Limbic system - involved in emotions and memory
clinicalFacts: The adult human brain weighs approximately 1.3-1.4 kilograms
The brain contains billions of neurons
The brain consumes a large proportion of the body's oxygen supply

heart.name: Heart
heart.description: The heart is a muscular pump that circulates blood throughout the body. It maintains oxygen delivery, nutrient transport, and removal of metabolic waste.
anatomy: Right ventricle - pumps blood to lungs
Left ventricle - pumps blood to the body
Heart valves - regulate blood flow direction
clinicalFacts: The heart beats around 100,000 times per day
The left ventricle is the strongest chamber

lungs.name: Lungs
lungs.description: The lungs are respiratory organs responsible for exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood.
anatomy: Left lung contains two lobes to accommodate the heart
clinicalFacts: The lungs contain millions of alveoli
The right lung is slightly larger than the left lung
Gas exchange occurs through the alveolar membrane

liver.name: Liver
liver.description: The liver is the largest internal organ and performs essential metabolic, detoxification, digestive and storage functions.
clinicalFacts: The liver can regenerate after injury
It performs hundreds of biochemical functions
It plays an important role in drug metabolism

kidney.name: Kidney
kidney.description: The kidneys are filtering organs that maintain fluid balance, remove waste, regulate electrolytes and help control blood pressure.
functions: Produces hormones involved in red blood cell production
clinicalFacts: Each kidney contains many filtering units called nephrons
